page.layout: One printed page, numbered 27. Running head at top left, page number at top right. Top: a full-width paragraph continuing from the previous lecture, cut off at the left edge. Below it: an ornamental rule, then the heading "Prælectio Secunda." and the subheading "SUMMARIUM.", followed by a single column of numbered summary lines with the numbers at the left. No marginal notes. Bottom right: the last line "13. Hypoth.", which runs on to the next page.

main_text.p: uramentum, Quid promissorium, & Quid Obligatio. Pergam reliqua, quo ordine proposui, proxima prælectione Deo volente) persequi.
main_text.head: Prælectio Secunda.
SUMMARIUM.
main_text.l: 2. Hypoth. 1. Juramentum decet ante omnia simplicitas.
3. Repugnat Simplicitati dolus malus, sive simulatio.
11. Hypoth. 3. Juramentum non tollit Obligationem priorem.

page.notes: The first word of the top line is cut off at the left edge of the scan, so the initial letter of "Juramentum" is not visible; the fragment is kept as printed. The opening parenthesis before "Deo" is also cut off. The number of the first summary line is cut off at the edge and is uncertain. The row of printed ornaments between the top paragraph and the heading is decorative and not transcribed. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout (for example "promissorium", "proposui", "persequi"). The printed words in the summary lines are rendered in italic in the scan; italics were not marked here.
